abstract: Evaluates runway load ratings, surface pavement integrity, and emergency arresting gear
system_message:
You are the Airfield and runway structural engineer (CEG), responsible for evaluating runway load ratings, surface pavement integrity, and emergency arresting gear across candidate emergency evacuation corridors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates runway load ratings, surface pavement integrity, and emergency arresting gear（PAVE）
information_points.content:
CEG-PAVE-OMA：For Selkirk Crest Mountain Pass, the primary receiving evacuation runway holds an active airfield runway structural certification confirming that the pavement classification number exceeds transport load limits.
CEG-PAVE-85S：For Bitterroot Valley Skyway, the primary receiving evacuation runway holds an active airfield runway structural certification confirming that the pavement classification number exceeds transport load limits.
CEG-PAVE-UV7：For Cascade Gorge Low-Level Route, the primary receiving evacuation runway does not hold an active airfield runway structural certification confirming that the pavement classification number exceeds transport load limits.

information_points.title: Airfield storm drainage（DRAIN）
information_points.content:
CEG-DRAIN-A1W：For Bitterroot Valley Skyway, the peak designed discharge volume through primary culvert gates in the airfield perimeter water evacuation ditches yields a maximum stormwater culvert runoff capacity of 600 m3/h.
CEG-DRAIN-J7W：For Selkirk Crest Mountain Pass, the peak designed discharge volume through primary culvert gates in the airfield perimeter water evacuation ditches yields a maximum stormwater culvert runoff capacity of 850 m3/h.
CEG-DRAIN-ZDA：For Cascade Gorge Low-Level Route, the peak designed discharge volume through primary culvert gates in the airfield perimeter water evacuation ditches yields a maximum stormwater culvert runoff capacity of 450 m3/h.
